_comment: Hand-curated short meaning blurbs for the pin renderer. Used when the Wikipedia auto-extractor returns nothing. Keys are name slugs (lowercase, hyphenated). Each value should be ≤80 characters and avoid non-Latin scripts.
ava: Latin origin; possibly from avis (bird) or a short form of Eva.
jacob: Hebrew Ya'aqov, 'supplanter' or 'holder of the heel'.
owen: Welsh Owain, often linked to Latin Eugenius, 'well-born'.
julian: Latin Iulianus, from the Roman family Julius.
grayson: English surname, 'son of the grey-haired one'.
greyson: English surname, 'son of the grey-haired one'.
jayden: Modern American coinage, often linked to Hebrew Jadon ('thankful').
lincoln: English place name, from Latin colonia at Lindon ('lake colony').
hudson: English surname, 'son of Hud' (a medieval form of Hugh).
jaxon: Modern respelling of Jackson — 'son of Jack'.
jaxson: Modern respelling of Jackson — 'son of Jack'.
maverick: American English, 'independent-minded', from rancher Samuel Maverick.
elias: Greek form of Elijah — Hebrew, 'my God is YHWH'.
axel: Scandinavian form of Absalom — Hebrew, 'father is peace'.
jordan: Hebrew Yarden, 'to descend' — the river name.
austin: Medieval English contraction of Augustine — Latin, 'venerable'.
brooks: English surname, 'one who lives by the brook'.
kai: Multiple origins; Hawaiian 'sea', Welsh 'keeper', Frisian short form.
atlas: Greek myth — the Titan condemned to hold up the sky.
atticus: Greek Attikos, 'from Attica' (the region around Athens).
bennett: Medieval English form of Benedict — Latin, 'blessed'.
callum: Scottish Gaelic Calum, from Latin columba, 'dove'.
declan: Anglicised form of Irish Deaglán, an early saint's name.
emmett: English surname from Emma — Germanic ermen, 'whole, universal'.
knox: Scottish surname, from Old English cnocc, 'round hill'.
luca: Italian form of Luke — Greek Loukas, 'from Lucania'.
phoenix: Greek Phoinix — the mythic fire-bird that rises from ashes.
ryker: Dutch surname Rijker, from Germanic ric, 'ruler'.
tate: Old English Tata, an affectionate pet name; later 'cheerful'.
waylon: American English, popularised by Waylon Jennings — 'land by the road'.
wyatt: English surname Wyot, from Old English wig + heard, 'brave in war'.
ella: Germanic short form of names with the element ali, 'other, foreign'.
scarlett: English occupational surname, 'seller of scarlet cloth'.
camila: Latin Camilla — Roman name for a young attendant at a religious ritual.
penelope: Greek — wife of Odysseus, possibly from pēnē, 'weft thread'.
aurora: Latin, 'dawn' — Roman goddess of the morning.
eleanor: Old Provençal Alienòr, possibly from Greek elea, 'mercy'.

ivy: English plant name, from Old English īfig.
